FINDING_ID: LB_F001
SEVERITY: 0.90
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.8
DESCRIPTION: The LoadBalancer's greedy solver and F1 feasibility checks are structurally decoupled from the probabilistic feasibility gate. `_solve_greedy` and `_check_feasibility` allocate token load up to the static limit `m.L`. However, the Codex timeout addition requires `P(feasible) >= feasibility_threshold` (default 0.90) for dispatch. If a model has `L_std > 0`, an allocation packed to `m.L` yields `P(feasible) = 0.5`. Since $0.5 < 0.90$, the LoadBalancer actively generates allocations that are mathematically guaranteed to be blocked at dispatch, leading to infinite reallocation loops or dropped tasks.
PROPOSED_FIX: In `LoadBalancer._solve_greedy` and `LoadBalancer._check_feasibility`, replace static limit checks (e.g., `current_loads[m_idx] + demands[j] <= limits[m_idx]`) with the native probabilistic gate: `self.dispatch_check(self.models[m_idx], current_loads[m_idx] + demands[j])[0]`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F002
SEVERITY: 0.85
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.6
DESCRIPTION: In `DynamicManager.process_round()`, cost distribution artificially destroys the efficiency metric (`mu`) of healthy models. Total `round_cost` is divided proportionally by output length (`len(resp.content)`). If a model times out or fails (producing 0 content), its assigned cost becomes 0. The financial and compute cost of the timeout is shifted entirely onto the successful models. This causes false-positive diminishing returns signals because successful models appear to become massively more expensive.
PROPOSED_FIX: Distribute `model_cost` using `responses[mid].response_time` (which accurately captures compute time burned during a timeout) or distribute it based on the allocated `token_demand` established by the LoadBalancer, completely discarding output length as a cost proxy.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F003
SEVERITY: 0.80
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.7
DESCRIPTION: `CapabilityFingerprint.as_normalised_array` inverts `D_decay` (a "lower is better" metric) *after* normalizing by `pool_max`. This mathematically compresses capable pools. If models have excellent, near-zero D_decay values of 0.01 and 0.02, `pool_max` is 0.02. Normalization yields [0.5, 1.0], and inversion yields [0.5, 0.0]. The model with D_decay=0.02 receives a zero capability score for that dimension, penalizing it identically to a model with an absolute worst-case D_decay of 1.0.
PROPOSED_FIX: Invert `D_decay` prior to normalization. Update `CapabilityFingerprint.as_array()` to return `[1.0 - self.D_decay, self.v_bar, self.A, self.C]`. `_compute_pool_max` will then automatically capture the maximum "goodness", and `as_normalised_array` can cleanly execute `raw / pool_max` without secondary inversion.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F004
SEVERITY: 0.70
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.5
DESCRIPTION: In `RoleAssignment.reassign()`, the condition that assigns the Collator (COL) role evaluates `len(self._models) >= 3`. Because `self._models` references the static initial pool, this constraint never updates. If unrecoverable failures (e.g., EXCLUDE policy) permanently reduce the active model count to 2, the framework improperly forces a COL role instead of degrading to the mathematically required K < 3 state (1 PM, N PAR).
PROPOSED_FIX: Modify the hysteresis guard in `reassign()` from `if len(self._models) >= 3:` to `if len(active_models) >= 3:`.
VERIFIED: TRUE
